newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary again says no deal soon on NATO fighters.
newsitem.headline: Hungary again says no deal soon on NATO fighters.

text.p: Hungarian Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti repeated on Monday that Hungary would not be rushed into buying NATO-compatible fighter aircraft, saying no tender was likely until the end of this year at the earliest.

"I think the position of the Hungarian government is quite clear and that is we will wait for a NATO decision on enlargement," Keleti said at a joint news conference with visiting Swedish Defence Minister Bjorn von Sydow.

"If we are invited for negotiations (to join NATO)...it will make the situation clear and then we will publish a tender, but I do not think it will be before the end of this year," Keleti added in response to a question.
NATO will hold a meeting in Madrid in July during which at least three countries, Hungary, Czech Republic and Poland, are expected to be asked to join the Western military alliance.
Von Sydow said Sweden was committed to remaining outside NATO but added "in all other respects we are very ambitious to develop relations with NATO countries and non-NATO countries".

Sweden's Wallenberg group, which produces the JAS 39 Gripen fighter, is among several European and American defence contractors which have been lobbying hard for Hungary's order to replace aging MiG fighters with NATO-compatible equipment. Hungary last year seemed on the verge of placing an order, but decided to delay.

"The minister did not come here as a representative of the Wallenberg group," Keleti said. "But I told him why we decided to delay the preparation of the fighter tender and he accepted the reasons with understanding."

Keleti also sought during the news conference to dispel confusion over a $100 million contract Hungary has signed with France's Matra Defense Espace, a subsidiary of Lagardere Group, to purchase air defence missiles.
An independent commission has declared that the Defence Ministry violated the law when it pursued talks exclusively with Matra after February 20, Hungarian media have said.
Keleti said the contract itself was legal, but the complaints about it would have to be adjudicated.
"No one is questioning the contract itself...but we should wait for a written decision and I would think we are going to go to court over it," he said.

Keleti said von Sydow would stay until Wednesday for consultations on defence issues. He added that he had told von Sydow the reasons behind Hungary's decision not to take part in the Italian-led mission in Albania and had discussed other issues concerning the Balkans.
